notes.evidence: Script: review-work/gnome-guest-closure-provenance/openpgp_check.py. What it does: dearmors the signature block and checks CRC24; parses the v4 signature packet; dash-unescapes the text, strips trailing spaces/tabs and joins lines with CRLF without the final line ending; hashes that text, then the hashed prefix, then the 0x04 0xFF + length trailer; checks the left-16 bits; computes RSA m = s^e mod n; compares against an exact EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 SHA-512 DigestInfo. Result: one signature packet per file, type 0x01, RSA, SHA-512, issuer fingerprint F6ECB376...C93C. For each file: left16 match = True and RSA_PKCS1v15_VALID = True. Negative control (one bit flipped in the canonical text) gives verifies = False. release-02 (noble) has 30 lines with trailing whitespace and still verifies, so the canonicalization step was exercised. The CI's gpgv records command-1621/1622/1623 agree: exit 0, stderr 'Good signature from "Ubuntu Archive Automatic Signing Key (2018)"', 'using RSA key F6ECB376...C93C', signature times 2026-10-30 19:32:31, 2024-04-25 15:11:21 and 2026-10-30 04:02:35 UTC.

notes.title: The bootstrap leaves a SYSTEM logon task and a startup entry in the guest; it disables no security feature
notes.claim: In specialize, running as SYSTEM, the bootstrap does four things. It creates C:\ProgramData\JappHarness with a protected ACL (SYSTEM and Administrators Full, Users ReadAndExecute, inheritance off). It registers the scheduled task JappOwnedMachineAttestation (SYSTEM, RunLevel Highest, AtLogOn, 1-minute limit), which runs machine-attestor.ps1 from that directory. It writes a Default-profile Startup JappFixture.cmd that runs the guest controller as the standard user. The attestor sets Winlogon AutoAdminLogon=0 and AutoLogonCount=0 and removes DefaultPassword. All of these persist only inside the disposable guest. The protected ACL stops the standard fixture user from changing the SYSTEM-run script. Nothing changes Defender, firewall, UAC, SmartScreen, BitLocker, the boot configuration or the persistent execution policy: `-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned` is process-scoped and appears only on the command line.
notes.evidence: Full read of the three files, plus a case-insensitive grep for web, socket and http APIs, URLs, Defender/MpPreference, firewall/netsh, reg add, bcdedit, EnableLUA/ConsentPrompt, SmartScreen, credential/SecureString/password/token/cmdkey, Set-ExecutionPolicy, services, WinRM/ssh, Remove-Item, disk formatting, Start-Process, Invoke-Expression, encoded commands, Add-Type and DllImport. The only hits are the items listed here, loopback HTTP and sockets, and the Add-Type/DllImport of the reviewed windows11_owned.cs. My view that a standard user cannot rename C:\ProgramData children rests on my knowledge of the default ProgramData ACL; I did not observe it.

verified.title: Recorded runner_image_version differs from the job-log Runner Image header
verified.claim: host-tools-lock.json records runner_image_version "20261026.354.1", which windows11_candidate.stage_host reads from the ImageVersion env var. The GitHub log header for the same download-only job says Runner Image ubuntu-24.04 Version 20261025.353.1, and its Included Software and Image Release links point to ubuntu24/20261025.353. The GNOME prepare download-only job 124399194862 shows the same split: header 20261025.353.1, lock 20261026.354.1. The win11 authorize job header also says 20261025.353.1. The consumer (windows11_vm.install_tools) compares the lock value with os.environ['ImageVersion'], so the check compares like with like and fails closed. Two separate runners show the same split, so it looks systematic rather than tampering (inferred). The release record should still say the bound value is the env-reported ImageVersion and is not the image release GitHub's header names. The campaign will also refuse to run once hosted runners no longer report ImageVersion 20261026.354.1, so the release window is limited.

What I checked:

(2) At S (a5ec1e3), windows11_candidate.py:214 writes this field from os.environ.get("ImageVersion") (constant at line 39). windows11_vm.py:116-120 (install_tools) raises ValueError when lock["runner_image_version"] != os.environ.get("ImageVersion"). The GNOME code does the same: ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:247 writes the field, and ubuntu_gnome_host.py:95 and ubuntu_gnome_vm.py:538 compare it. Every producer and consumer reads the same environment variable, so the check compares like with like and fails closed, including when the variable is missing (None != string).
(3) Job logs, fetched with read-only `gh api`: the Windows 11 download-only job 124399778731, the GNOME download-only job 124399194862, the GNOME authorize job 124399014009 and the Windows 11 authorize job 124399335264 all print "Runner Image / Image: ubuntu-24.04 / Version: 20261025.353.1", with Included Software and Image Release links to ubuntu24/20261025.353. The ubuntu-24.04 package build job 124396495513 and doctor+verify job 124383475702 from run 41149738856 print the same header.

What remains: the release receipt should label runner_image_version as the env-reported ImageVersion, not the GitHub header or release tag. That is a documentation and accuracy note for a record not yet written. No change to the candidate is needed.
